engagement: I commit before God to follow this course to the end.

ecrans.html:
This course does not want to fill your head. It wants to change your life. The lessons, the questions, the exercises and the sheets are there for that: so that what you learn passes into the way you live.

It lasts six months, the time to finish all the modules. Then comes the Mise en Action (Putting into Action), six more months in which you apply what you have learned, with support.

It asks you to change habits. If you are looking for a course to read from time to time, this is not the one. You will be pushed, and that is intended. Christ called us to freedom, not to indiscipline: “Exercise yourself toward godliness… godliness has value in all things, having the promise of the life which is now, and of that which is to come” (1 Timothy 4:7-8).

• I do every assignment. No excuses, but no silence either: if I am stuck, sick or traveling, I notify my corrector before disappearing, with the “Report an unavailability” button at the bottom of the home screen.
  • I accept being followed. My corrector and the coordinators see where I am: my modules, my sheets, my ticked boxes. They never see what I write in my evening review or in my personal journals. My follow-up is based on my ticked boxes in “My day.”
  • I accept being called back. If my progress stops, I will be called, without being judged, to understand and help me get going again.
  • I accept being pushed.

During the training, I set aside what scatters me: TV series, worldly books and films, outings and chatting with friends who are not moving in the same direction. Here is the minimum for each day. Doing more is a good thing.

  • Sleep 7 to 8 hours, never less than 6. Go to bed around 9:30-10 p.m., get up around 5:30 a.m. No sleeping pills, no phone in bed, no sleeping in. A short nap in the afternoon is good. If my way of life makes this impossible, I talk to my trainer.
  • Pray three times, at least 15 minutes each time. Morning and evening at a set time and in a set place. In the afternoon, even while working.
  • Stay in contact with God all day long: thank, praise, worship, with spiritual music near me if possible.
  • Read the Bible every day, following the course’s reading calendar. Allow about 1 to 2 chapters, that is 10 to 15 minutes. The whole New Testament during the training, the whole Bible at least once a year.
  • Take part in the Monday prayer communion, from 11 p.m. to midnight, online. This is where all the builders, wherever they are, pray together.
  • Do the evening review and the plan for the next day.

The morning (30 min to 1 h): thank and worship, say my declaration, command the day, pray in the spirit (if I do not yet have tongues, sing and worship), pray over my goals, meditate on a passage.
The afternoon (30 min): worship and pray in the spirit.
The evening (30 min to 1 h): review, thanksgiving, prayer in the spirit, reading the Bible, a course or a Christian book.

My evening review comes down to four questions. What did I do with my 12 hours: what I had planned, what I did, what I missed? What successes, what failures, what disappointments? What surprise opportunities did I seize or miss, and why? What lesson do I keep for tomorrow?

A few verses for commanding the morning

“Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.” (Ephesians 5:16)

“For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith. Who is he who overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God? […] We know that whoever is born of God doesn’t sin, but he who was born of God keeps himself, and the evil one doesn’t touch him.” (1 John 5:4-5, 18)

“Then you shall return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him who serves God and him who doesn’t serve him.” (Malachi 3:18)

“Tell the righteous ‘Good!’ For they shall eat the fruit of their deeds. Woe to the wicked! Disaster is upon them; for the deeds of his hands will be paid back to him.” (Isaiah 3:10-11)

“Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place, that it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and shake the wicked out of it? It is changed as clay under the seal, and presented as a garment. From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.” (Job 38:12-15)

“Though a sinner commits crimes a hundred times, and lives long, yet surely I know that it will be better with those who fear God, who are reverent before him.” (Ecclesiastes 8:12)

“For evildoers shall be cut off, but those who wait for Yahweh shall inherit the land. For yet a little while, and the wicked will be no more. Yes, though you look for his place, he isn’t there. But the humble shall inherit the land, and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace. The wicked plots against the just, and gnashes at him with his teeth. The Lord will laugh at him, for he sees that his day is coming. The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, to kill those who are upright on the path. Their sword shall enter into their own heart. Their bows shall be broken.” (Psalm 37:9-15)

My declaration. I learn it by heart and say it morning and evening, every day, until the end of the training. It is in the “My day” tab.

My phone. A smartphone is desired, according to my needs and my means. No need for a luxury model: money has better uses, and it is better to learn to make it bear fruit before living in luxury. I need at least a Bible app and an app for reading digital books (PDF, ePub).

Three rules:

  • No phone in the morning before my devotion. If I read the Bible on it, I first put it in airplane mode.
  • Airplane mode during times of worship and Bible study, at church or elsewhere.
  • I completely cut off the Internet at certain times each day, so that my heart does not stay attached to the phone and social media.

My checklist. During the six months, the checklist that counts is the one in “My day,” in this application. The ABBA Life one is optional during the training. I will pick it up again when I have finished the course.
